messages:
alex: FYI noticed a p99 uplift (~12%) on host ingress after the kernel-selector change last night. Mostly for small HTTP/gRPC chat requests that stream tiny frames.

marta: ugh. observed same in canary dashboards. traces show a new memcpy on the gRPC read path around our preparse stage. can you paste the flame?

alex: flame attached (excerpt). top stacks: 
```
30%  grpc/read -> http2/frame_unmarshal -> host_preparse_copy -> tokenize
18%  host_preparse_copy -> kvcache/lookup -> kvcache_miss
9%   http2/read_frame -> syscall(read)
```
looks like the kernel selector path changed buffer ownership, forcing us to copy into a contiguous buffer before tokenize.

sam: that matches a local repro i ran. small payloads (~200-600B) now allocate+copy into a new buf before tokenization. previously we did zero-copy parse into mmap'd slab.

kevin: any idea which diff introduced it? build-bot shows a rollout of kernel-selector v2 at 3223334200.

build-bot: deploy: kernel-selector v2 -> service/host-preparse at 3223334200. canary promoted 3223334380.

marta: suspect change in the kernel->runtime handshake: buffer shape changed for aligned kernels. when buffer isn't contiguous we were falling back to host_preparse_copy.

alex: profiler also shows KV cache churn: small requests are creating per-fragment keys (client_id+seq+small-frag) causing high eviction rate. kvcache miss cost added to p50 too.

sam: patch idea: (1) restore zero-copy path for HTTP2 small frames when frame length < 1KB and frame is single-window; (2) change kernel-selector to return a borrowed slice flag so preparse knows it can read in-place; (3) consolidate fragment keys to stable prefix for tiny requests to reduce kvcache thrash.

kevin: agree. also tweak batching heuristics: current mini-batch timer is too aggressive for small requests — it tries to aggregate but forces a precopy window. propose: for small payload routes set batch_timeout shorter and favour immediate dispatch without copy.

alex: i'll prototype the borrowed-slice flag. quick sketch: 
```
struct BufferRef { ptr: *u8, len: usize, owned: bool }
// kernel-selector returns owned=false when backing memory is stable for the request lifecycle
```
then host_preparse only copies if owned==true.

marta: add tests for mapped vs owned buffers. also add a kvcache sim for fragment-key collision to validate the consolidation fix.

sam: i ran a canary with the borrowed-slice change locally — p99 down ~9%, allocations dropped by 45% for the micro-test. pushing a PR now.

alex: nice. can you include microbench script and a small curl/http2 harness? also check gRPC streaming edge: multi-frames might still require copy for reassembly.

sam: will do. i'll special-case single-frame streaming and have reassembly path remain unchanged. PR: https://git.internal/r/12345 (WIP)

kevin: post-merge checklist: (a) roll canary to 10% for 30m, (b) watch p50/p95/p99 for chat route, (c) check kvcache hitrate graphs for tiny-requests cohort.

alex: sounds good. created an infra alert to auto-rollback if p99 increases >5% from baseline.

marta: thanks — also add a telemetry tag (kernel_selector=v2_fix) so we can slice traces.

build-bot: ci: tests passed for PR 12345 on linux-amd64, unit coverage +1%.

sam: PR updated with tests and docs. moving to review.

alex: great work. once merged we should see the host-side overhead go back to pre-roll numbers and smooth out kvcache churn. I'll follow up with a short postmortem if the fix lands.
